knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to divide the total costs and income by billable hours, so the rate is recovered from work that can be billed. Dividing by all paid hours or copying a competitor's rate does not do this.
The lesson says travel, set-up and clean-down do not shrink with the length of the treatment, so a minimum charge covers the time needed to reach the client and start work.
The lesson says to use your own costs and billable hours first, then compare with local evidence. A national average, a friend's rate or one bidding listing is not a sound source.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find the billable hours.
